metadata.title: The Three-Quote Addendum
metadata.description: A municipal procurement analyst dies suddenly shortly after flagging irregularities in a routine IT hardware renewal. The paper trail looks ordinary until workstation logs and document metadata reveal a second set of hands.
metadata.briefing: A city procurement analyst collapsed at home hours after emailing concerns about a vendor addendum. Your first leads are mundane: a workstation login trail and a document whose metadata doesn’t match its story.

assets.title: City Email Export: IFB 2026-IT-014 Addendum 2 Distribution (Victim Mailbox)
assets.description: Exported email thread from the victim’s city mailbox showing the distribution of “IFB 2026-IT-014 Addendum 2 Clarification” at 18:26 and a vendor reply at 18:39 referencing the quoted model (BST-14G). The messages document when the addendum became official and what vendor immediately benefited from the specification language.

assets.description: City IT custody/inventory form documenting the assigned custodian for workstation asset tag MAD-WS-04419. The record notes the last logged-in user as EVELYN.PARK with a timestamp of 2026-03-18 16:58.

emails.from: Madison Police Department (MPD) - Central District Investigations
emails.subject: Assignment Briefing — “The Three-Quote Addendum” (Financial Crime / Suspicious Death)
emails.body:
Det. Moreno,

We are opening “The Three-Quote Addendum,” a Financial Crime / Suspicious Death case tied to a sudden death of a municipal procurement analyst shortly after she flagged irregularities in a routine IT hardware renewal. The procurement file reflects that “Addendum 2 - Laptop Refresh” was distributed from the victim’s city email account that evening, after she indicated she was pausing tabulation pending review.

Digital artifacts indicate the distributed addendum PDF was produced via “Microsoft Print to PDF” and carries an embedded author tag (“oschultz”) with a creation time consistent with the after-hours window. Separately, forensic review of the victim-assigned workstation (MAD-WS-04419 / last logged-in user EVELYN.PARK) shows recent-run data consistent with generating/printing the addendum document at roughly the same minute as the PDF creation, supporting that the addendum-generation workflow occurred on the victim’s endpoint.

What remains uncertain is who had hands on the keyboard at that workstation, how access was obtained (e.g., unattended session vs. other means), and how the suspected procurement manipulation intersects with the death scene beyond proximity in time. A witness statement from the neighbor who called 911 anchors the medical emergency and indicates no obvious trauma was observed, but the circumstances of the death are still being treated as suspicious pending investigative development.

This matters now because the alleged addendum manipulation appears timed to influence an imminent award recommendation and because the compromised addendum originated from the victim’s account, creating a risk of ongoing procurement exposure and possible follow-on misconduct. Immediate objective: lock down and corroborate the chain from building access opportunity to workstation activity to addendum distribution, and identify all individuals with plausible access and motive during the narrow after-hours window (including confirming movements and communications around the addendum send).

MPD Central District Investigations

emails.subject: RE: IFB 2026-IT-014 — Addendum handling tonight
emails.body:
Detective Moreno,

I want to put on record what I told Evelyn earlier on 2026-03-18: I explicitly instructed her not to send any addendum that night and to hold it for my review the next morning.

I left the City-County Building before the evening events and did not return. If any addendum went out at 18:26, it was not at my direction.

— Mara Kline
City Procurement Officer

emails.subject: Availability 3/18 evening — IFB 2026-IT-014
emails.body:
Det. Moreno,

Re: the timeframe when the addendum was emailed, I was tied up during that window. At 18:09 on 2026-03-18 I posted in the “Procurement-IT-014” Teams channel: “I’m on a call—back in ~30.” That was during my scheduled “Vendor demo - Zoom” from 18:00–18:30 (meeting ID 845 221 9031).

I wasn’t handling Evelyn’s workstation or sending anything from her account at 18:26.

— Lena Hart
Municipal Procurement Analyst

emails.subject: Preservation notice — CCB North Doors badge events 2026-03-18 evening
emails.body:
Det. Alicia Moreno,

Per your request, Facilities is preserving the City-County Building access-control export for “CCB 215 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd - North Doors” covering 2026-03-18 evening. The export includes badge activity showing “OWEN SCHULTZ” on badge ID ending “-1173” with an entry at 18:03 and exit at 18:31.

We are holding the relevant access-control data to prevent routine overwrites while your investigation is active.

— CCB Facilities / Access Control Desk

emails.subject: Metadata Analysis Results — Custody Record (MAD-WS-04419) Device Correlation
emails.body:
Detective Moreno,

We completed the requested metadata analysis of the submitted City IT custody/assignment record (document.custody_form_mad_ws_04419) associated with workstation asset tag **MAD-WS-04419**.

The record documents that the **Last Logged-in User** was **EVELYN.PARK**, with a **Last Logged-in Timestamp** of **2026-03-18 16:58 (America/Chicago)**. The record note indicates this precedes the incident window anchored at **2026-03-18 19:12**.

For device/timeline correlation purposes, we also incorporated the canonical forensic artifact supplied with the request: the Windows registry key **HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU** on MAD-WS-04419 reportedly contains entry **'b' = 'AcroRd32.exe /p /h "C:\\Users\\EVELYN.PARK\\Desktop\\Addendum2_LaptopRefresh.docx"'**, with **MRUList "ba"** and **LastWriteTime 2026-03-18 18:12:40**.

These observations support a linkage between the endpoint identifier (MAD-WS-04419), the victim profile identifier (EVELYN.PARK), and the timed print-to-PDF workflow artifact. Per standard limitations, this correlation does **not** establish the human operator, and recorded metadata can be modified by software, copying, or system processes.

A formal report has been uploaded to the case file.

suspects.name: Owen Schultz
suspects.relationship: Worked with the victim on municipal IT hardware refresh coordination
suspects.motive: The laptop refresh recommendation was due the next morning, and the victim had just paused tabulation after questioning addendum language that would narrow eligible models. If the discrepancy was escalated, it could have disrupted the award path and exposed who had been pushing the restrictive requirement into the process.
suspects.alibi: He says he was at the City-County Building in the early evening to pick up a printout and discuss a last-minute addendum issue, then drove to the victim’s home for a brief “check-in” about the confusion. Building badge logs can independently confirm his entry and exit window, but there is no neutral third-party record that accounts for his movements between leaving the building and later that night.
suspects.background:
Owen Schultz is the IT Services asset manager responsible for tracking and coordinating device deployments and refresh planning.

His work regularly intersects with procurement on hardware specifications and timelines, and he has routine access to the procurement floor at the City-County Building.

He is familiar with shared city imaging tools and the day-to-day handling of workstation profiles and printing workflows.

suspects.name: Derek Yazzie
suspects.relationship: Primary vendor contact for the city’s laptop refresh bid; worked with the victim on bid questions
suspects.motive: Badger State Tech’s quoted model (BST-14G) matched the restrictive requirement that appeared in the addendum, and Derek had a direct professional incentive to see that specification adopted. With the award recommendation memo scheduled for the next morning, he also had reason to push for language that would keep competitors out without reopening the whole solicitation.
suspects.alibi: He states he was at Badger State Tech’s office during the evening and can produce sent-email records showing a reply from d.yazzie@badgerstatetech.com at 18:39 acknowledging the specification; his employer’s building access logs can confirm entry/exit times. The limitation is that those records confirm his messaging and presence at the office, not what communications he may have had by phone earlier in the day.
suspects.background: Derek Yazzie is the account executive handling the City of Madison’s laptop refresh solicitation for Badger State Tech Supply. A vendor reply email from his address at 18:39 thanks the city for a specification that aligns with the model his company quoted (BST-14G). His role gives him familiarity with the bid documents, timelines, and who at the city was coordinating addenda and clarifications.

suspects.name: Lena Hart
suspects.relationship: Colleague who worked with the victim on quote comparisons for the laptop refresh
suspects.motive: Lena was under pressure to keep the laptop refresh on schedule and may have wanted to avoid a restart of scoring that could add late nights and public scrutiny. She also had an interest in keeping the comparison spreadsheet clean and consistent, even if that meant pushing a clarification through quickly.
suspects.alibi: She reports she was on a scheduled “Vendor demo - Zoom” from 18:00–18:30 and posted in the “Procurement-IT-014” Teams channel at 18:09 that she was on a call and would be back in ~30. This can be independently checked via calendar and Teams exports, though it does not by itself confirm where she was physically located during the call.
suspects.background:
Lena Hart is a procurement analyst who collaborated with the victim on quote comparisons for IFB 2026-IT-014.

Her work routinely involves reviewing vendor submissions, reconciling specs, and coordinating with internal stakeholders during active bid tabulations.

On the evening of 2026-03-18, her collaboration records show she was engaged in a scheduled vendor demo during the narrow window when the addendum was distributed.

suspects.name: Mara Kline
suspects.relationship: Victim’s supervisor on the laptop refresh solicitation
suspects.motive: She had professional incentive to keep the IFB timeline orderly and avoid a late-night addendum that could trigger vendor protests or a restart. She also had reputational pressure to ensure the solicitation didn’t appear mismanaged after the victim paused scoring late in the day.
suspects.alibi: Building badge logs show she exited the City-County Building at 17:11 on 2026-03-18 with no later entries, which can be independently checked against access-control records. This does not account for her movements off-site after leaving the building.
suspects.background:
Mara Kline is the City of Madison Procurement Officer overseeing the IT laptop refresh solicitation and had formal authority over addenda issuance.
On 2026-03-18 at 17:22, she emailed the victim instructing: “Do not send any addendum tonight—hold for my review in the morning.”
Her building access history for that date shows entry at 07:54 and exit at 17:11, with no recorded re-entry that evening.

timeline.event: At 4:42 PM, the victim sent an internal message that she was “pausing tabulation pending an addendum review.”
At 6:26 PM, an addendum PDF was emailed from the victim’s city account to the bid distribution list as a ‘clarification.’
At 9:03 PM, 911 was called for an unresponsive adult at the victim’s address; EMS noted no obvious trauma.

actions.message: Lab results are in. Next, compare the device-correlation findings against the access log and call/chat records to identify which account activity aligns with the flagged device and timeframe.
Use the correlation report to build a timeline. Cross-check the report’s timestamps with the access log, then validate communications around those times in the call log and chat export.
Preservation is in place. Document chain-of-custody for any new artifacts you review, and prioritize corroborating logs (access/call/chat) before drawing conclusions from statements.

forensicOutcomes.conclusionText: Metadata analysis of the submitted City IT custody/assignment record (document.custody_form_mad_ws_04419) supports correlation between workstation asset tag MAD-WS-04419 and the victim user profile EVELYN.PARK, including a recorded last logged-in timestamp of 2026-03-18 16:58 (America/Chicago). When considered alongside the provided forensic artifact describing RunMRU activity at 2026-03-18 18:12:40 for a print-to-PDF workflow referencing C:\Users\EVELYN.PARK\Desktop\Addendum2_LaptopRefresh.docx, the record supports a device/user-timeline linkage but does not establish the human operator.

questions.prompt: When was Addendum 2 first distributed from the victim’s city email account?
What after-hours badge entry window is shown on 2026-03-18 (entry/exit times)?
Which vendor and model were said to benefit from the addendum specification language?
Which RunMRU print-to-PDF entry and LastWriteTime link the addendum path to the EVELYN.PARK profile on MAD-WS-04419?

solution.explanation: After the victim paused tabulation over a suspiciously restrictive requirement, “Addendum 2” was still sent from her account at 18:26, implying someone used her environment to make the change and push it out quickly. The PDF’s own properties tag the author as “oschultz” with a creation time of 18:12, and independently, building badge records put Owen Schultz inside the City-County Building from 18:03–18:31, exactly spanning the creation-and-send window. The decisive link is the forensic device-correlation: on the victim’s assigned workstation (profile EVELYN.PARK), the RunMRU registry shows an Acrobat print-to-PDF command targeting “Addendum2_LaptopRefresh.docx” at 18:12:40, aligning to the PDF’s 18:12:44 creation time and tying the authored file to the victim’s machine. While this artifact cannot prove the human at the keyboard (metadata can be manipulated and the analysis primarily links device, profile, and time), the combination of the “oschultz” author tag plus Owen’s verified physical presence eliminates coincidence. The strongest red herring—vendor Derek Yazzie—explains motive (the spec matched his quoted model) but the record shows the restrictive language originated from the city-side send, not his mailbox. Lena Hart and Mara Kline are resolved by time-stamped records placing Lena on a concurrent call and showing Mara absent from the building after 17:11 and explicitly instructing not to send an addendum that night, leaving Owen Schultz as the only suspect supported by both opportunity and the correlated workstation-forensic trail.
